what_this_is: The registry of every program / competition database the engine can draw on. One entry per source. Adding a new activity means: drop the raw file in data/, add an entry here, and (only if its shape is unusual) write a small adapter in compass/programs.py. Nothing else in the engine changes.
contract: Every source resolves to rows in the common programs schema (see data/programs.csv header). A source that cannot fill `activity`, `name` and either `level` or `kind` is not usable — fix the adapter rather than loosening the schema.
ladder_note: The rungs a credential can climb. Step 6 (Two Paths) uses exactly this vocabulary to build a stretch path by INTENSIFY — same activity, next rung up. Any new source must map its levels onto these six words, not invent its own.

sources.name: Hand-verified program catalog
sources.coverage: Programs verified by hand, one family at a time. Currently Bay Area heavy.
sources.refresh: continuous — every verified recommendation should land here
sources.known_gap: Thin. When it has nothing for a task the engine falls back to a live verified web lookup, which costs a call per recommendation and cannot be reviewed ahead of time. Growing this file is the cheaper fix.

sources.name: Tabroom circuits
sources.coverage: US speech & debate circuits with 2026-27 tournament counts, by state.
sources.refresh: annual — tournament counts change each season
sources.note: Tournament count is how live a circuit is, not how hard it is. It ranks circuits; it never becomes a claim about the student.

sources.coverage: Not yet sourced. Wanted: team/event listings by state with the progression from local qualifier to championship.
sources.url_note: Left blank on purpose — a URL enters this file only after someone has opened it and confirmed what it contains. Same rule the engine applies to recommendations.

how_to_add_a_source: 1. Put the raw file in data/ under its own name. Never edit it to fit — the adapter does the fitting.
2. Add an entry here with status 'active', the activities it covers, and verified_on.
3. If its columns already match programs.csv, set adapter to 'programs_csv' and append the rows. Otherwise add a function to ADAPTERS in compass/programs.py that yields rows in the common schema.
4. Map its levels onto the six ladder rungs. If something genuinely does not fit, raise it rather than adding a seventh rung — the stretch logic in Step 6 depends on this ladder being ordered.
5. Run the coverage check: python -c "from compass import programs; print(programs.coverage())"
